summary: This Dockerfile creates a Docker image based on Ubuntu 24.04 and installs a collection of development tools and Python libraries needed to run a Python application. It then copies an app.py file into the container and sets up the environment to run that Python script when the container starts.

explanations.1: This special comment tells Docker to use an advanced syntax version that supports newer Dockerfile features.
explanations.4: The && chains multiple commands together so they all run as one layer; if any command fails, the whole RUN stops instead of continuing.
explanations.15: After installing packages, we clean up the package manager cache and delete temporary files to make the final image smaller.
explanations.18: The --break-system-packages flag tells pip to install packages even though Ubuntu normally discourages installing packages this way in its system Python.
explanations.26: CMD specifies the default command that runs when the container starts — in this case, it will execute 'python3 app.py'.
